snippet.title: the ICELAND vlog
snippet.description:
May 2015 -  I went to Iceland. These are all of my Iceland videos combined into one. Check out the description for travel details!
All of my Iceland vlogs were shot on this Sony RX100 - http://amzn.to/2s2g7mD
✨LINKS & INFO👇🏻

ICELAND VIDEOS / PICTURES
Vlog 1: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VABRw5Kpi0w
Vlog 2: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OcwIApFRArg&feature=youtu.be
Vlog 3: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lm47Uzhuw2c
Iceland Short Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lUXppjq9VqI
Iceland BTS Part 1: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZbDzQWBB0lw
Iceland BTS Part 2: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6HJ1pzIW8Sc
Iceland DSLR pics: https://www.flickr.com/photos/114041146@N05/albums/72157653997363189
Iceland iPhone pics: https://www.flickr.com/photos/114041146@N05/albums/72157656299899638

STOP 1 
Upon arriving at the airport we were picked up by Rent a Car Reykjavik and hopped in our dope red Jeep.  It had four wheel drive which really came in handy.  We started with a long drive up to the Westfjords.
TIP: Gas is expensive. About $6.33/ gallon so budget for gas.
MOST BEAUTIFUL DRIVE OF MY LIFE.  We went to Iceland at the beginning of the summer (MAY) so there was still snow on the majority of the mountains in the Westfjords region.  
Our first stop was Flateyri - it was pretty much a ghost town but our Air Bnb was just adorable and there was a bigger town close by where we ended up spending a good amount of time (Isafjordur, Iceland).
TIP: You will be fine with paying credit card everywhere but make sure to register a PIN for it before you leave the states.
We spent our first two days in this region.  The drives were glorious, the towns were beautiful and there was a pretty epic waterfall close by… (Dynjandi Water Fall)

STOP 2
Stykkishólmur was one of my favorite parts of this trip and the drive there was so dreamy.  If you are familiar with The Secret Life of Walter Mitty this is actually the “Greenland” town that he visits then takes off from in a helicopter. It was amazing to actually be where those scenes took place.
There is a large hill you can hike up next to the harbor and see the entire town.  The view held me captive for two hours. 
Some places we also visited during this part of our trip: Kirkjufell (waterfall & mountain), Arnarstapi (arch on the coast), and the Snæfellsnes peninsula.  

STOP 3
Reykjavik is such a fabulous city and we got to experience a lot of it being there for 4/5 days.  Concert we went to -- Alt-J
Tip:  Even if you have a four wheel drive car don’t get too cocky when it comes to snow. We got stuck. What got us out -- toggling a switch called "traction control" who knew.
It was super stressful; however, it turned out to be one of the most memorable places we went.  It was so GREEN and I truly felt like I was on a different planet.  It makes for a good story.
Tip: Don’t blindly trust a Garmin GPS. When it comes to landmarks (i.e. waterfalls, mountains, etc.), look them up before-hand and get the directions from humans that have been there before.  
Going up to the top of the church was unreal.  The views were unforgettable and I am in love with how colorful the town is.

- Kevin Long, the dyrt, https://thedyrt.com/ 
The Dyrt is all about making searching for campgrounds and guided adventure trips a better experience. Through beautiful technology and an amazing community of outdoor enthusiasts, The Dyrt ends the pain of searching for campgrounds and guided adventure trips.


- Anis Mojgani, Poet, http://thepianofarm.com/
Anis Mojgani is a two time National Poetry Slam Champion, winner of the International World Cup Poetry Slam, and multiple-time TEDx Speaker. He has been awarded residencies from the Vermont Studio Center, AIR Serenbe, and the Oregon Literary Arts Writers-In-The-Schools program. Anis has performed at numerous universities, festivals, and venues around the globe and has performed for audiences as varied as the House of Blues and the United Nations. His work has appeared on HBO, NPR, and in the pages of such journals as Rattle, Forklift Ohio, Paper Darts,Thrush, and Bat City Review. 
Anis is the author of three poetry collections, all published by Write Bloody Publishing: Songs From Under the River, The Feather Room, Over the Anvil We Stretch. His latest book, The Pocketknife Bible, is a fully illustrated poetry-memoir. Originally from New Orleans, Anis currently lives in Oregon and is represented by Blue Flower Arts.

snippet.title: NEW YORK CITY shot on iPhone 7 Plus
snippet.description:

[PREV VIDEO] "a little encouragement" - http://bit.ly/SomeEncouragement

*AUDIO* all audio was recorded by iphone. no external devices were used.

*FRONT FACING CAMERA* the selfie camera was used when talking to it. i did not use the rear camera for these shots.

*STABILIZATION* no warp stabilization was applied in post. just the built in IS in the iPhone and my dope camera work :)

READ - With so much craziness going on in the world lately it was kind of hard editing a vlog about something like Snapchat. Seems pretty insignificant compared to everything else but hopefully this is ten minutes of entertainment or inspiration or something and then go back out into the world and love love love. We all have our own circle of people that we can influence and inspire and just LOVE on. Nothing you do is insignifcant so keep making art, working hard and being a light into other's worlds. Buy someone coffee, compliment a stranger, call your grandma IDK just be the love you want to see in the world. LOVE YOU PEACHY FAM.

CREATIVE SPACES TV QUESTIONS

Q: How do you come up with the questions? Do you write them down?
A: I have a phone conversation with them on the phone before to get to know them better and then formulate some questions from that convo but once I'm there I just turn it into a conversation - no notes or anything. Really depends on the interviewer I think. But I've found they are most comfortable when it's most similar to a normal conversation!

Q: Lighting?
A: All natural light. Traveling with a lighting rig is hard :) HOWEVER - I do use a big reflector. Helps a lot.

Q: How did you do the title?
A: Multiple "Creative Spaces TV" titles in different colors spread out and spaced on the premiere timeline to flickr. Not a very graceful way - but no special effects.

Q: How does external audio stay synched through cuts?
My interview videos are each one big clip - so I line up via multi cam sequence in premiere. So click on the two interview angles + good audio and right click to put in multicam sequence. After that I LINK the video with new audio so they stay together when I start cutting and splicing.

snippet.title: Neon Camera Bag Hack
snippet.description:
Inside of most camera bags & camera gear = both black. Doesn't make sense!
[PREV VID] Q&A with my mom! http://bit.ly/QAJeannie

I might play around with it some more. Maybe get some bright duck tape or something. Long story short - this was fun and might work better with different spray paint that I used! Or just buy a bag with a non-black interior ha. 

If you're curious about the spray paint it's called Montana Gold Acrylic Spray Paint

snippet.title: PREVIEW | iPhone 6S Plus Video Test (Low Light, Slow Motion & Image Stabilization)
snippet.description:
INITIAL THOUGHTS:  I was looking forward to testing out the built in image stabilization in the iPhone plus.  All of this was shot handheld; I was pretty impressed. Some of the beginning shots where I was filming while walking across the street the shot was very bumpy but the iPhone kept the shot very steady. The only downside was there was a lot of the jello effect (0:13).  I cut around it but it is still noticeable. Just don't expect something from a steadicam when you are filming while walking / running. 

Inside the record store (& obviously the concert) was very dark.  From this video you can deduce that the iPhone really shines with the proper lighting and not the given conditions.  It does not help that I was shooting at a higher frame rate AND in low light conditions.  It definitely put a lot of pressure on the sensor but I look forward to doing a proper video test with the iPhone 6S+.  Hopefully I can prove that you don’t need a fancy video camera to shoot awesome stuff.  But you do need a fancy video camera if you want to get great shots in low light.
